newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli-PLO talks resume despite Hebron attack.
newsitem.headline: Israeli-PLO talks resume despite Hebron attack.

text.p: Senior Israeli and Palestinian negotiators resumed talks on the fate of Hebron on Wednesday despite a shooting attack by an Israeli soldier that wounded seven Arabs in the West Bank town, a PLO official said.
"The talks have restarted," the official told Reuters.
PLO and Israeli security sources said Israeli Defense Minister Yitzhak Mordechai began talks with chief PLO negotiator Mahmoud Abbas at the home of U.S. Ambassador Martin Indyk.

"The meeting is aimed at trying to finalise the remaining oustanding issues and to prepare for a summit meeting between President (Yasser) Arafat and (Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin) Netanyahu," said PLO negotiator Jamil al-Tarifi.
Netanyahu's office said in a statement the diplomatic efforts of U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross could lead to a Netanyahu-Arafat summit Wednesday night or Thursday.

"Ross met this afternoon with Yasser Arafat following the phone conversation between Arafat and the prime minister," the statement said. "Ross reported to the prime minister by phone that it appears that a meeting will take place between the prime minister and Arafat tonight or tomorrow."

An off-duty Israeli soldier sprayed bullets at Palestinian shoppers in a produce market in the heart of Hebron on Wednesday in an attempt to sabotage the imminent handover of 80 percent of the West Bank city to PLO self-rule.
The gunman, Noam Friedman, said he wanted Hebron to remain entirely in Jewish hands forever and expressed no remorse for the attack.
PLO officials said on Tuesday talks on implementation of the Hebron deal signed last year by the PLO and Israel's previous left-leaning government had been concluded.

They said Mordechai and Abbas were due to discuss oustanding interim issues from the 1995 accord other than Hebron, including fixing dates for further Israeli redeployments from the West Bank and the release of Palestinian prisoners.
Netanyahu and Arafat condemned the shooting and vowed to continue peace talks despite the attack.
